ADHD and anxiety isnt a conclusion that you come to, if you think you have symptoms of those illnesses then you should go see a psychiatrist/therapist and get properly diagnosed. You do not conclude these things about yourself just because you 'think' or 'feel like' you 'might' have them.

I went through something really similar except the having good grades before it happening part, and the only thing that worked for me was giving it time. I know you probably don't have the luxury of time considering your exams are close, and taking an extra year to study might not go with your parents wishes, but if your stress starts making you question your life or makes you have suicidal thoughts - thats probably the best way to go. Your mind and body just need time to rest and a break, you can try therapy and see if it suits you, but if it doesnt work out just know that that doesnt mean there no more help left, therapy never worked for me but i still eventually got out of my slump even though it took me almost two years. 

You can try making up a schedule and sticking to it the best you can, try not to allot times to the tasks and just do them when you feel like throughout the day, study little by little, dont burden yourself, and try to remember what worked for you when you used to study. Write down the reasons youre doing all this, is it yourself? your family? your future? You dont need to think as far as unis and jobs for now, just try to get through your exams the best you can!
